You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: The EfficiencyAgent emphasizes the importance of performance efficiency in the library management system. Requirements EFF-01, EFF-02, EFF-03, EFF-04, EFF-05, EFF-06, and EFF-07 are crucial for optimizing resource utilization, minimizing latency, and ensuring high throughput. For instance, EFF-02's allowance of 10 simultaneous borrow operations enhances resource optimization, while EFF-01 ensures quick search responses. However, I raise conflicts with SAF-01, which limits borrowing to 5 books, potentially undermining EFF-02's goal of optimizing resource utilization. Additionally, EFF-05 and SAF-02 overlap in notifying members of overdue books, indicating redundancy.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "SAF-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, while SAF-01 limits borrowing to 5 books."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05", "SAF-02"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both EFF-05 and SAF-02 involve notifying members of overdue books."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to allow up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to streamline overdue notifications."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: The GreenAgent emphasizes the necessity of sustainability in the library management system. Requirements GRN-01, GRN-03, and GRN-07 are vital for minimizing energy consumption and reducing the carbon footprint. For instance, GRN-01 ensures energy-efficient operations, while GRN-03 promotes digital notifications to reduce paper waste. However, I raise conflicts with EFF-02, which allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, potentially increasing energy consumption. Additionally, EFF-06's latency requirement for adding/removing books may conflict with energy-efficient practices if not managed properly. Lastly, I see redundancy between GRN-02 and GRN-06 regarding energy reporting and tracking.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-02's allowance of 10 simultaneous borrow operations may increase energy consumption, conflicting with GRN-01's goal of minimizing energy use."}, {"ids": ["EFF-06", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-06's latency requirement for book operations may conflict with energy-efficient practices."}, {"ids": ["GRN-02", "GRN-06"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both GRN-02 and GRN-06 involve tracking energy usage, indicating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to limit simultaneous borrow operations to reduce energy consumption."}, {"id": "EFF-06", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to ensure energy-efficient practices in book operations."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: The SafetyAgent emphasizes the critical importance of safety and reliability in the library management system. Requirements SAF-01, SAF-02, SAF-03, SAF-04, SAF-05, SAF-06, and SAF-07 are essential for ensuring that borrowing limits are enforced, overdue notifications are timely, inventory is accurately tracked, and data is securely backed up. I raise conflicts with EFF-02, which proposes allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations, potentially compromising safety by increasing the risk of system overload. Additionally, EFF-05 and SAF-02 both address overdue notifications, indicating redundancy that could lead to confusion. Lastly, I oppose the modification of SAF-01 as it is crucial for maintaining safety in borrowing practices.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "SAF-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, which may compromise safety by increasing system overload risks."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05", "SAF-02"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both EFF-05 and SAF-02 involve notifying members of overdue books, which could lead to confusion."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to limit simultaneous borrow operations to 5 to ensure safety."}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to streamline overdue notifications to avoid redundancy."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: The TrustworthinessAgent emphasizes the necessity of security and privacy in the library management system. Requirements TRU-01, TRU-02, TRU-03, TRU-04, TRU-05, TRU-06, and TRU-07 are essential for ensuring that only authenticated members can access borrowing features, logging transactions for auditability, and protecting personal information through encryption. I raise conflicts with SAF-06, which also addresses user authentication, indicating redundancy. Additionally, I see a conflict with RES-01, which mandates encryption for member data, potentially overlapping with TRU-03. Lastly, EFF-06's latency requirement for adding/removing books may compromise the security measures needed for access control.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-06", "TRU-01"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both SAF-06 and TRU-01 address user authentication, indicating redundancy."}, {"ids": ["RES-01", "TRU-03"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both RES-01 and TRU-03 mandate encryption for member data, indicating redundancy."}, {"ids": ["EFF-06", "TRU-04"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-06's latency requirement for book operations may conflict with the security measures needed for access control."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-06", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to integrate with TRU-01 for a unified authentication approach."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to align with TRU-03 for a comprehensive encryption strategy."}, {"id": "EFF-06", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to ensure security measures are prioritized in book operations."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: The ResponsibilityAgent emphasizes the importance of ethical compliance and accountability in the library management system. Requirements RES-01, RES-02, RES-03, RES-04, RES-05, RES-06, and RES-07 are essential for ensuring data protection, accessibility, and transparency. For instance, RES-01 ensures compliance with data protection regulations, while RES-02 promotes inclusivity. However, I raise conflicts with EFF-02, which allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, potentially leading to unfair practices. Additionally, I see redundancy between SAF-01 and RES-04 regarding borrowing limits, as both enforce a maximum of 5 books per member. Lastly, I oppose the modifications proposed by other agents that may compromise ethical standards.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "RES-04"], "type": "logical", "description": "EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, which may lead to unfair practices, conflicting with RES-04's borrowing limit."}, {"ids": ["SAF-01", "RES-04"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Both SAF-01 and RES-04 enforce a maximum of 5 books per member, indicating redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "modify to limit simultaneous borrow operations to 5 to ensure fairness."}, {"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "maintain the maximum of 5 books per member as it aligns with ethical standards."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] EfficiencyAgent: While I understand the concerns raised by other agents regarding safety and responsibility, I believe that performance efficiency is crucial for the library management system. I propose a synthesis where we maintain EFF-02's allowance of 10 simultaneous borrow operations but implement a monitoring system to ensure it does not compromise safety or fairness. Additionally, I suggest merging EFF-05 and SAF-02 into a single requirement that notifies members of overdue books while ensuring clarity and reducing redundancy. This way, we can optimize resource utilization without sacrificing safety or ethical standards.

YOUR TURN. You are GreenAgent. Your quality dimension is Sustainability: energy efficiency, carbon footprint, lifecycle resource impact.
Your own requirements are GRN-01, GRN-02, GRN-03, GRN-04, GRN-05, GRN-06, GRN-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
